column1: # HEINRICH LEIBHOLZ DIED IN KREUZBERG, NOT IN THE BOROUGH HE LIVED IN —
# AND THAT IS WHY HIS WIDOW IS FOUND THERE NINE YEARS LATER.
# Landesarchiv Berlin, Standesamt Kreuzberg, P Rep. 510 Nr. 667, Namensverzeichnis zum Sterberegister
# 1948, page 180, under the AUGUST heading. Found 8 October 2026. Confirmed at the image.
field
*** LEIBHOLZ · HEINRICH · 2493 · 9. [AUGUST 1948] ***
column2: STERBEREGISTER KREUZBERG 1948 NR. 2493. The Bemerkungen column prints the day only, under a month heading, and it runs in step with the register numbers either side of him: Lücke verw. Maase 1.8.1948 / 2441 · Liebigski 31.7.48 / 2445 · Langner geb. Bremer 5. / 2464 · Lehmann verw. Golchert 8. / 2477 · *** LEIBHOLZ, Heinrich, 9. / 2493 *** · Lange verw. Gärtner 11. / 2504 · Lenz verw. Martin 11. / 2517. THE BARE "9." IS 9 AUGUST 1948. Crop at site/public/heinrich-leibholz-kreuzberg-1948.png.

column1: and it confirms a date this archive had only on somebody else's authority
column2: Mapping the Lives gives Heinrich "† 09.08.1948" with no source for the death beyond the 1939 census card. THE REGISTER NOW SAYS THE SAME DAY IN ITS OWN HAND, and the archive has an OFFICE AND A NUMBER for the first time.

column1: # ---------------- WHY NEUKÖLLN DID NOT HAVE HIM, AND WHY THAT NEGATIVE WAS RIGHT ----------------
HIS ADDRESS WAS NEUKÖLLN AND HIS DEATH WAS NOT
column2: the 1939 census has him at LEINESTRASSE 32 III. rechts, Neukölln, and the Berliner Adressbuch has him there 1938 to 1942. NEUKÖLLN'S 1948 DEATH INDEX WAS READ PAGE BY PAGE AT THE IMAGE ON 8 OCTOBER — P Rep. 380 Nr. 700, L/1948 pages 357 to 371, Januar through Dezember with the August heading on 367 — AND IT IS CORRECTLY EMPTY. A DEATH REGISTERS WHERE IT HAPPENS, NOT WHERE THE DEAD PERSON LIVED, and this is that rule with a name attached.

column1: the ordinary explanation, stated as a reading and not a finding
column2: THE URBAN-KRANKENHAUS STANDS IN KREUZBERG DIRECTLY ON THE NEUKÖLLN BOUNDARY, a few minutes from Leinestraße. A man of fifty-seven taken there would register in Kreuzberg. THE INDEX DOES NOT SAY WHERE HE DIED and this archive is not claiming a hospital; the certificate gives the place of death and will settle it.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT IT DOES FOR AGNES, WHICH IS WHY THE SWEEP WAS RUN ----------------
*** IT PLACES THE HOUSEHOLD IN KREUZBERG IN AUGUST 1948, NINE YEARS EARLIER THAN ANY RECORD HELD HERE ***
column2: AGNES LEIBHOLZ née KERGER is at MEHRINGDAMM 109, KREUZBERG, in the Berlin directories from 1957 and in the telephone books to 1979-80 — and this archive had NO IDEA WHY THE FAMILY WAS IN THAT BOROUGH. She is in Neukölln on census night 1939 and in Kreuzberg by 1957 with nothing in between. THE BOROUGH CONNECTION BEGINS WITH HER HUSBAND'S DEATH, NOT WITH HER FLAT.

column1: *** AND THE CERTIFICATE IS THE FIRST DOCUMENT ABOUT AGNES THIS ARCHIVE COULD EVER HAVE ***
column2: A 1948 Berlin death entry names the SURVIVING SPOUSE, the INFORMANT and the DECEASED'S ADDRESS. Everything held about Agnes is a census card and a line in a directory. STERBEREGISTER KREUZBERG 1948 NR. 2493 is orderable by number through service.berlin.de. *** A PURCHASE, AND DAVID'S TO MAKE. *** It is the cheapest thing on the list and the only one that reaches her directly.

column1: # ---------------- HOW THE SWEEP WAS RUN, AND ITS LIMITS ----------------
THE SCOPE WAS ALL OF BERLIN AND THAT WAS DELIBERATE
column2: He died on 9 AUGUST 1948 and THE MAGISTRAT DID NOT SPLIT UNTIL THAT NOVEMBER, so Berlin was still one city and a Neukölln man could have died in Mitte or Friedrichshain as easily as in Charlottenburg. Sweeping only West Berlin would have applied a border that did not yet exist. The catalogue was enumerated office by office: 29 OFFICES HOLD A 1948 DEATH INDEX, 41 VOLUMES, 6.5 GB.

column1: *** AND 40 OF THE 41 ARE BLIND ***
column2: the 1948 registers are handwritten and their text layers are empty. The single legible volume is Reinickendorf Nr. 1505, 51 pages, 1.06 MB, a supplement with nothing in it. SO THE SCAN'S VALUE WAS NOT ITS HITS BUT ITS MAP: it said which volumes could never be read by text, and the search was then RANKED instead of ground through from A to Z.

column1: how the ranking was chosen
column2: his own borough's unread second volume first; then WEDDING, because the JÜDISCHES KRANKENHAUS in the Iranische Straße is there and this archive already knows a Leibholz who died in it — GERTRUD, 27 February 1943 — and Heinrich was the Jewish partner of a Mischehe; then the adjacent hospital boroughs. HE WAS IN THE THIRD ONE OPENED.

column1: *** CLEARED ALONG THE WAY ***
column2: NEUKÖLLN Nr. 700, L/1948 pp. 357-371, nothing. NEUKÖLLN Nr. 701 — which turns out NOT TO BE A GENERAL INDEX AT ALL but the register of WAR DEAD, every entry a man with a 1942-45 date registered late; its L block (pp. 264-284) holds no Leibholz, nearest LEIBOLD. WEDDING 1948 Nr. 11, L block pp. 160-174, Januar to Dezember, nothing. SCHÖNEBERG 1948 needed no work at all — P Rep. 163 Nr. 583, pages 73 to 80, was read at the image in September and recorded in data/schoeneberg-1938-1968-instrument.tsv.

column1: *** AND ONE LIMIT STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED ***
column2: ONLY PAGE 180 OF KREUZBERG 1948 HAS BEEN READ. The L block runs roughly pages 168 to 196 and the REST OF IT IS UNREAD, so this file can say that Heinrich is in Kreuzberg 1948 and CANNOT say he is the only Leibholz in it. Reading the remaining pages is a short errand and is not done.

column1: a false alarm, recorded because it was raised
column2: while ranking the boroughs this archive briefly concluded that SCHÖNEBERG 1938-1948 HAD NEVER BEEN READ, because the resume pointer schoeneberg-progress.tsv tabulates only P Rep. 163 Nr. 584 onward — which begins in 1949 — while claiming "1938 to 1968 runs without a gap". THE CLAIM IS TRUE AND THE POINTER IS INCOMPLETE: the 1938-1948 years are in a DIFFERENT FILE, schoeneberg-1938-1968-instrument.tsv, year by year with page ranges. Nothing is wrong except that the pointer does not point at its own other half.
